messages:
arjun: Quick RFC follow-up on quantization/precision profiles (FP8/INT8/4-bit). I sketched an API surface + runtime changes but want alignment on quality tradeoffs, rollout, and telemetry. Major questions below.

maria: Can you paste the API sketch? want to see how this maps to routing/compat checks.

arjun: Sure — proposal: add an optional `quant_profile` on model config + per-request override. Profiles are named bundles: e.g. `fp8_perf`, `int8_balanced`, `4bit_aggressive`. Each profile specifies per-layer scheme, outlier handling, and fallback order. Example metadata: 

```json
{"quant_profile": "int8_balanced", "fallback": ["fp16","int8_stable"], "calibration_id": "cal-2026-02-15"}
```

devon: Important: runtime must expose kernel capabilities and a compatibility matrix (model arch x profile x HW). We already have kernel selectors but this adds per-profile selection + calibration artifacts. Ops will need to pre-warm caches for each profile.

eva: From ML side — quality tests need to be tied to calibration datasets and regression thresholds. We should record per-profile eval stats (perplexity, exact-match, hallucination markers) and gate rollouts automatically. Also per-profile deltas vs baseline FP16.

sarah: Product question — should `quant_profile` be opt-in or do we auto-suggest cheaper profile for cost-sensitive tiers? PLG users expect sane defaults.

arjun: My take: default = none (fp16) for safety. Redwood Optimize can surface recommended profiles per workload; users can opt-in at model config or per-request. For enterprise Reserved/Dedicated we can offer 'auto-suggest' with explicit acceptance.

maria: Runtime concerns on KV cache: mixing quantized vs non-quantized KV caches isn't safe unless we translate key/value formats. Need a migration strategy: either invalidate cache on profile switch or maintain per-profile KV namespaces. Both have cost. Thoughts?

devon: Per-profile KV namespaces seems simplest for correctness. We'll add a `kv_namespace` tag to requests derived from model+profile. Storage overhead but avoids subtle correctness bugs. We should also expose a TTL policy to GC unused namespaces.

arjun: Agree. Also calling out mixed precision per-layer: some models benefit from FP8 activations + INT8 weights. Profiles must express mixed-precision maps. That implies our kernel selector needs to support intra-op mixed precision, or we fallback to safest unified kernel.

eva: Calibration: we need a shared calibration store and reproducible quantization step. Calibration artifacts should be signed and tied to a model version+profile. For quality monitoring, run a rolling eval on production prompts (scrubbed) and alert if metric drift > threshold.

sarah: Rollout plan idea: 1) internal canary on synthetic traffic; 2) opt-in beta customers; 3) gradual traffic ramp with automatic rollback if eval regressions or latency SLO violations. Add telemetry flags to track per-profile P50/P95 token latency and token cost.

maria: Implementation notes for eng-runtime: add `profile` dimension to routing key, adjust autoscaler estimator (throughput changes), add kernel capability registry. Backwards compatibility: if profile requested but not available, follow profile.fallback order or reject with clear error code `QUANT_PROFILE_UNAVAILABLE`.

devon: Ops-bot suggestion: add deploy gating that checks calibration artifacts present on target nodes before enabling profile. If not present, auto-fetch from signed store. Also record node-level `supported_profiles` metadata.

ops-bot: incident-bot: reminder — add observability dashboards: per-profile error rate, latency, memory, and a quick drilldown for model+profile+region.

arjun: Two open tradeoffs we still need to pick: 1) default opt-in policy (none vs recommended) 2) cache migration approach (invalidate vs per-profile namespaces). Also need a small RFC section on calibration governance (who approves calibration artifacts). I'll draft a follow-up RFC patch with a proposed default policy and migration plan. Anyone want to take the calibration governance section?

eva: I'll own calibration governance and the eval criteria.

sarah: I'll write the customer-facing wording for recommendations and defaults.

maria: I'll sketch the kernel capability registry and the API for `QUANT_PROFILE_UNAVAILABLE` error codes.

arjun: Great — I'll open the RFC patch and assign sections. Thanks all, will sync next week. :thumbsup:
